title.zh: 折返夷门：邯郸被围那年，一个不肯白送的人
title.en: Turning Back at the Yimen Gate: The Year Handan Was Besieged, and the Man Who Would Not Give It Away Free

dek.zh: 魏安釐王二十年，秦军围邯郸，魏王遣晋鄙救赵，却因畏秦令晋鄙停军于邺观望，平原君的使者责问魏救不至。魏公子决意赴秦军而死，路过夷门辞别后又折返，被一个守门老人当面点破：那是拿肉投餒虎。本文看他如何在没有干净选项时准备、付代价、认亏欠。
dek.en: In the twentieth year of King Anxi of Wei, Qin's armies closed around Handan and the king of Wei sent General Jin Bi to relieve Zhao, but, fearing Qin, had him halt at Ye and wait to see which way things went; Lord Pingyuan's envoys complained that Wei's relief had not come. The Wei prince resolved to go and die at the Qin army; after taking his leave at the Yimen gate and riding off, he turned back, and an old gatekeeper told him to his face that this was meat thrown to a starving tiger. Here is how he worked the problem when no option was clean — what he prepared, what it cost, and what he admitted he owed.

heading.en: Messengers Who Would Not Stop Coming

paras.zh: 魏国公子（下称公子）的姐姐，是赵国平原君（赵惠文王之弟）的夫人。魏安釐王二十年，秦军击破赵长平军之后，进兵围住邯郸。魏王派将军晋鄙带十万众救赵。秦王遣使警告魏王：攻赵旦暮可下，诸侯有敢救赵的，拔赵之后必先移兵击之。魏王恐惧，派人叫晋鄙停军，驻扎在邺，「名為救趙，實持兩端以觀望」。平原君的使者冠盖相属，赶到魏国，责让公子：平原君说，自己之所以与公子结为婚姻，是看重公子的高义，以为公子能急人之困；如今邯郸旦暮之间就要降秦，而魏国的救兵至今不到，公子能急人之困又在哪里？末了还添一句「獨不憐公子姊邪」。难处在于：救兵听命于魏王，而魏王畏秦，按兵不动。
paras.en: The Wei prince's elder sister was the wife of Lord Pingyuan of Zhao (younger brother of King Huiwen of Zhao). In the twentieth year of King Anxi of Wei, after Qin had broken Zhao's army at Changping, its armies pressed on and encircled Handan. The king of Wei sent General Jin Bi with a hundred thousand troops to relieve Zhao. The king of Qin sent an envoy to warn the king of Wei that Zhao would fall any day, and that whichever of the lords dared to relieve it, Qin would turn its troops on first once Zhao was taken. The king of Wei, afraid, sent orders halting Jin Bi, who encamped at Ye — nominally relieving Zhao, in fact keeping a foot in both camps and waiting to see. Lord Pingyuan's envoys arrived in Wei one after another — caps of office and carriage canopies in an unbroken line — reproaching the prince: Lord Pingyuan said he had joined himself to the prince by marriage because he valued the prince's high sense of duty and believed him a man who would rush to others in distress; now Handan was within days of surrendering to Qin, and Wei's relief still had not come — where, then, was that readiness to rush to others in distress? They added, in translation: had he no pity for his own sister? The difficulty: the relief army answered to the king of Wei, and the king, fearing Qin, kept it standing still.

paras.zh: 此时公子手里有三千门客，却未被任以国政。他多次请魏王出兵，宾客辩士也「說王萬端」，魏王畏秦，终不听。公子自度终不能说动魏王，不肯独自活着而坐视赵亡，于是约车骑百余乘，打算带门客赴秦军，与赵俱死。出城路过夷门时，他向夷门守门人侯嬴（下称侯生）辞决。
paras.en: At this point the prince had three thousand retainers but no appointment to the governance of the state. He petitioned the king of Wei again and again, and his guests and persuaders argued with the king in every way; the king, fearing Qin, would not listen. Judging that he could never win the king over, and unwilling to live on while Zhao perished, he gathered a hundred-odd carriages and horsemen, meaning to go with his retainers to the Qin army and die together with Zhao. On his way out of the city, passing the Yimen gate, he took his leave of Hou Ying, the gatekeeper of the Yimen.

heading.zh: 三千门客与一个守门人
heading.en: Three Thousand Retainers and One Gatekeeper

paras.zh: 魏公子在魏国以养客知名。《史记》说他「公子為人仁而下士，士無賢不肖皆謙而禮交之」，不敢以富贵骄士，以致食客三千人，方圆数千里的士人争相投奔。这些门客不只是排场：有一回他和魏王下棋，北境举烽报警，说赵寇将入界，公子说是赵王田猎，不久北边传话果然如此。魏王问何以知晓，他说门客中有人能得赵王阴事。
paras.en: The Wei prince was known in Wei for keeping retainers. The Grand Historian writes, in translation, that he was humane and humble toward men of talent, treating every scholar, worthy or not, with courtesy and respect, never presuming on wealth and rank — so that he had three thousand retainers, and men of ability from a radius of several thousand li competed to attach themselves to him. They were not mere pageantry. One day, while he was playing a board game with the king of Wei, beacon fires on the northern frontier signaled a Zhao raid about to cross the border. The prince said the king of Zhao was out hunting, nothing more. Word later came from the north confirming exactly that. Asked how he knew, he explained that among his retainers was a man who could ferret out the king of Zhao's private business.

paras.zh: 一种解释是，这件事两面都算数：公子的信息能力得到验证，代价也记在账上——「是後魏王畏公子之賢能，不敢任公子以國政」。他越能干，魏王越不敢把国政交给他。等到邯郸告急，他没有国政之任，只能一再请王出兵；而原文给出的魏王终不听的缘由，是「魏王畏秦」。
paras.en: One reading is that the episode cuts both ways. His intelligence was proven — and the price went straight onto the ledger: in translation, from then on the king of Wei feared the prince's ability and dared not entrust him with the government of the state. The more capable he appeared, the less his king would hand him. By the time Handan cried for help he held no charge of the governance of the state and could only petition the king to send troops, again and again; and the reason the source gives for the king's refusal is his fear of Qin.

paras.zh: 公子敬重的另一个人，在夷门。侯嬴年七十，家贫，做大梁夷门的守门人。公子要厚赠，他不肯受，说自己「脩身絜行數十年，終不以監門困故而受公子財」。公子于是置酒大会宾客，空出车左的上位，亲自驾车去迎。侯生穿着破旧衣冠，径直上车坐了上座，不让，公子执辔愈恭。到家引他坐上座、遍赞宾客，满座皆惊。
paras.en: The other man the prince honored kept the Yimen, a gate of Daliang. Hou Ying was seventy, poor, and gatekeeper there. The prince called on him and wanted to make him a handsome gift, but he would not accept: in translation, he said he had kept himself and his conduct clean for decades and would not take the prince's money just because a gatekeeper's life left him poor. So the prince laid on a feast for his assembled guests, and when everyone was seated he drove out himself with his carriage and escort, leaving the seat of honor at the left of the carriage empty, to fetch Hou Ying in person. The old man turned up in his shabby clothes and worn cap, climbed straight into the seat of honor without yielding it, while the prince held the reins ever more respectfully. At home he seated Hou Ying in the place of honor and introduced him one by one to the assembled guests. The whole company was astonished.

paras.zh: 侯生后来把话说穿：他故意让公子的车骑久立市中，自己去拜访一位客人，借此观察公子，公子愈恭，于是「市人皆以嬴為小人，而以公子為長者能下士也」。他还推荐过一位屠者朱亥，说「此子賢者，世莫能知」。公子几次登门去请，朱亥不回谢，公子当时只觉得奇怪。作者认为，这些看似闲棋的往来，邯郸被围那年全用上了。
paras.en: Hou Ying later spelled out the game he had been playing. He had deliberately kept the prince's carriage standing in the marketplace while he called on an acquaintance of his, so as to watch the prince: the longer the prince waited, the more deferential he became — and so, he said in translation, the townsfolk all took Hou Ying for a petty man, and the prince for a true elder who could humble himself before men of talent. He also recommended a butcher named Zhu Hai, calling him, in translation, a worthy man whom the world did not know. The prince called on Zhu Hai several times; the butcher never came to return the courtesies, which the prince at that point simply found odd. In the author's view, all of these seemingly idle moves came due in the year Handan was besieged.

heading.en: From a Death Ride to Seizing an Army

paras.zh: 平原君的使者在魏国把话说绝：救兵不到，公子的高义安在。他多次请魏王，宾客辩士也百般劝说，魏王终不听；公子「自度終不能得之於王」，这才决意赴秦军而死。
paras.en: Lord Pingyuan's envoys left nothing to the imagination in Wei: with no relief army in sight, where was the prince's famed righteousness? He petitioned the king of Wei again and again, and his guests and persuaders argued every angle, but the king would not listen; only when the prince judged that he could never win the king over did he resolve to go and die against the Qin army.

paras.zh: 那天他出城，路过夷门，见到侯生，把要去秦军送死的打算讲了，辞决而行。侯生只说一句「公子勉之矣，老臣不能從」。车行数里，公子心不快——这是《史记》的叙述用语——说：「吾所以待侯生者備矣，天下莫不聞，今吾且死而侯生曾無一言半辭送我，我豈有所失哉？」他「復引車還，問侯生」。
paras.en: That day he rode out, passed the Yimen gate, stopped to see Hou Ying and told him the whole plan — going to die at the Qin army — then took his leave and set off. Hou Ying said only, in translation, that the prince should push on, and that this old servant could not follow him. A few li on, the prince felt displeased — the narrator's own phrase — and said, in translation, that he had treated Hou Ying handsomely in every way, as all the world knew; now he was going to his death, and Hou Ying had not half a word to see him off — had he fallen short somewhere? So he turned his carriage around and went back to question Hou Ying.

paras.zh: 作者认为，这一折返是全篇的转折。侯生当面把话挑明：「今有難，無他端而欲赴秦軍，譬若以肉投餒虎，何功之有哉」——没有别的办法，只想冲进秦军，等于拿肉喂饿虎，白送，还要门客何用。他还说，公子待他厚，此去而他不相送，公子必会「恨之復返」。他自己说：「以是知公子恨之復返也」。
paras.en: In the author's reading, that turn is the pivot of the whole story. Hou Ying put it to his face, in translation: with disaster upon him and no other plan, the prince meant to throw himself at the Qin army — like throwing meat to a starving tiger; what would it accomplish? Nothing gained — and what use, then, are retainers? He added that the prince had treated him well, and he had not seen the prince off; from this, he said, he had known the prince would resent it and come back.

paras.zh: 侯生给出的方案：他说，他听闻晋鄙的兵符常在魏王卧内，如姬最幸，出入卧内，有办法窃取。他又说，他听闻如姬的父亲被人所杀，三年未能报仇，自王以下想替她报父仇的都没能做到；她曾向公子泣诉，公子使客斩了仇人的头敬献给她。侯生说如姬「欲為公子死，無所辭，顧未有路耳」，所以公子开口请她，她必许。得虎符、夺晋鄙军，北救赵而西却秦，「此五霸之伐也」。公子从其计，去请如姬，「如姬果盜晉鄙兵符與公子」。
paras.en: Hou Ying's plan, as he laid it out: he said he had heard that Jin Bi's army tally — a tiger tally — was normally kept in the king of Wei's bedchamber, and that Lady Ruji, the king's favorite, came and went there and was able to steal it. He went on: he had also heard that her father had been murdered; for three years she had sought revenge, and no one, from the king down, had been able to avenge him. She had wept to the prince, who sent a retainer to cut off her enemy's head and presented it to her respectfully. Hou Ying said she was ready to die for the prince and would refuse him nothing; only, in translation, she had not yet had the opportunity. If the prince would but ask, she would certainly agree. Then, with the tiger tally in hand, he could seize Jin Bi's army, relieve Zhao in the north and drive Qin back in the west — in translation, an achievement to rank with the Five Hegemons. The prince followed the plan and asked Lady Ruji; she did indeed steal Jin Bi's army tally and give it to him.

paras.zh: 计策只管前半，后半是坏情况。侯生提醒「將在外，主令有所不受」：就算合符成功，晋鄙不交兵权、再向魏王请示，事情就危险了。带上屠者朱亥，「晉鄙聽，大善；不聽，可使擊之」。公子听完流泪，说「晉鄙嚄唶宿將，往恐不聽，必當殺之，是以泣耳，豈畏死哉」——照他自己的说法，哭的是非杀晋鄙不可，不是怕死。朱亥说自己是市井鼓刀屠者，从前不回谢是以为小礼无所用，「今公子有急，此乃臣效命之秋也」。侯生此前已说过老臣不能从，这里只请数着公子的行程，到晋鄙军那天「北鄉自剄，以送公子」。后来公子到了军中，「侯生果北鄉自剄」。
paras.en: The plan covered only the first half; the second half was the bad case. Hou Ying warned, in translation, that a general in the field does not accept every order from his sovereign: even with the tallies matching, if Jin Bi withheld the army and sent to the king instead, the whole enterprise would be in danger. So take the butcher Zhu Hai along: if Jin Bi obeyed, excellent; if not, Zhu Hai could be made to strike him. The prince wept on hearing it; in translation, he said Jin Bi was a battle-seasoned old general who he feared would not obey, and then he would have to be killed — that was why he wept, not because he feared death. By his own account, he wept over having to kill Jin Bi, not out of fear for himself. Zhu Hai said he was a butcher who wielded the knife in the marketplace; he had never returned the prince's visits because he thought petty courtesies were of no use — but now that the prince was in need, this was his moment to give his life. Hou Ying, who had already said at the gate that he could not follow, here only asked to count the days of the journey, so that on the day the prince reached Jin Bi's camp he would face north and cut his own throat, to see him off. When the prince did reach the army, Hou Ying did indeed face north and cut his own throat.

paras.zh: 公子到邺，矫魏王令代晋鄙。晋鄙合符之后起了疑心，举手看着公子质问：自己拥十万之众屯于境上，是国之重任，如今公子单车来代，这算什么？他「欲無聽」——侯生预想的坏情况果然出现。朱亥袖中四十斤铁椎，椎杀晋鄙。公子遂将晋鄙军，随即勒兵下令：「父子俱在軍中，父歸；兄弟俱在軍中，兄歸；獨子無兄弟，歸養。」得选兵八万人，进兵击秦军。
paras.en: At Ye the prince, on a forged royal order, moved to replace Jin Bi. Jin Bi matched the tallies but grew suspicious; raising his hand and looking at the prince, he asked, in translation, what it meant that he, holding a hundred thousand men on the frontier — a weighty charge of state — was now to be replaced by a man arriving with a single carriage. He was minded not to obey: the bad case Hou Ying had foreseen had come to pass. Zhu Hai, with a forty-catty iron mallet in his sleeve, struck Jin Bi dead. The prince then took command of Jin Bi's army and immediately issued an order to the troops, here in translation: where father and son were both serving, the father should go home; where brothers were both serving, the elder should go home; an only son with no brothers should go home and support his parents. He selected eighty thousand men and advanced against the Qin army.

paras.zh: 秦军解去，邯郸得救，赵国保住。赵孝成王与平原君亲到边界迎接，平原君背着箭袋在前引路，赵王再拜说「自古賢人未有及公子者也」，平原君不敢自比于人。
paras.en: The Qin army broke off and withdrew. Handan was relieved, Zhao preserved. King Xiaocheng of Zhao and Lord Pingyuan came out to the border to receive him in person, Lord Pingyuan carrying the quiver and arrow-case and leading the way. The king of Zhao bowed twice and said, in translation, that of worthies since ancient times none had been the prince's equal. At that moment Lord Pingyuan dared not compare himself with anyone.

paras.zh: 赵孝成王感念公子矫夺晋鄙兵存赵，与平原君商量以五城相封。公子的反应是「意驕矜而有自功之色」——仍是叙述用语。门客劝他：别人对公子的恩不可忘，公子对别人的恩最好忘掉；况且矫魏王令、夺晋鄙兵救赵，「於趙則有功矣，於魏則未為忠臣也」，自骄而居功，不可取。公子立自责，似若无所容者。后来赵王洒扫亲迎，执主人之礼，公子侧行辞让，「自言罪過，以負於魏，無功於趙」；赵王侍酒至暮，因公子退让，终究没有开口献出五城。
paras.en: King Xiaocheng of Zhao, grateful that the prince had seized Jin Bi's army on a forged royal order and saved Zhao, took counsel with Lord Pingyuan about granting him five cities. The prince's reaction, in the narrator's phrasing (here in translation), was a look of pride and self-congratulation. A retainer told him: some things must not be forgotten, others must be. Kindness done to the prince he should remember; kindness the prince had done to others, he should forget. And besides, forging the king of Wei's order and seizing Jin Bi's army to save Zhao was, in translation, a service to Zhao but not the act of a loyal minister to Wei — to swagger over such a credit was beneath him. The prince at once blamed himself, looking as if he had nowhere to hide. Later, when the king of Zhao swept the way, received him in person and performed the rites of a host, the prince stepped aside and declined, confessing, in translation, that he had wronged Wei and had no merit in Zhao; the king of Zhao served him wine until dusk but, because the prince held back so, never brought himself to offer the five cities.

paras.zh: 魏王怒公子盗兵符、矫杀晋鄙，公子自己清楚。原文紧接着记：退秦存赵之后，他派将领率军归魏，自己与门客留在赵国。这场救赵中盗符夺军、矫杀晋鄙的一段没有魏王的授权。
paras.en: The king of Wei was furious that the prince had stolen his tally and killed Jin Bi on a forged order, and the prince knew it. The source goes on directly: having driven off Qin and saved Zhao, he had a general lead the army back to Wei and stayed behind in Zhao with his retainers. The part of the rescue of Zhao in which he stole the tally, seized the army and killed Jin Bi carried no royal authorization.

paras.zh: 作者认为，把整件事拆开看，公子一次也不是在好与坏之间挑，摆在面前的是两条都不干净的路：赴秦军而死（侯生斥为「以肉投餒虎」）、矫令夺军（侯生所献，伤本国）。作者推断，侯生那句「以肉投餒虎」的作用，是逼他把勇气换成方案。作者提出的反事实：若他不折返，多半死在秦军阵前，邯郸未必得救，也不会有后来那支进兵的军队。
paras.en: In the author's reading, take the whole affair apart and the prince is never choosing between good and bad; what stood before him were two courses of action, both dirty: ride to die at the Qin army (which Hou Ying called throwing meat to a starving tiger), or forge an order and seize the army (proposed by Hou Ying; a wound to his own state). The author's inference is that Hou Ying's line about throwing meat to a starving tiger is what forced him to trade courage for a plan. The author's counterfactual: had he not turned back, he would most likely have died in front of the Qin lines, Handan might never have been relieved, and there would have been no army marching against Qin afterward.

paras.zh: 第二处是把坏情况写进计划。侯生提醒将在外、主令有所不受，于是朱亥随行、袖中藏椎，晋鄙听则已，不听则击。作者推断，这一步的难处不在敢不敢：公子听后的反应是流泪说，怕晋鄙不听，到时必须杀他，自己并非怕死。作者认为，从结果看，他欠了自己这方一笔债——杀本国宿将、盗王符、惹魏王怒——仍然把方案走完。原文记他事前已料到晋鄙恐不听、必当杀之；至于盗符、惹魏王怒等其他代价，原文没有写他事前是否掂量过。
paras.en: The second undignified spot is writing the bad case into the plan. Hou Ying's reminder that a general in the field need not accept every order put Zhu Hai at his side with a mallet up his sleeve: if Jin Bi complied, well; if not, strike. The author's inference: the hard part here was not daring. The prince's response on hearing the plan was tears — he said he feared Jin Bi would not obey, and that he would then have to be killed, and that he was not afraid to die. In the author's view, judging by the outcome, he took on a debt to his own side — killing his country's veteran commander, stealing the king's tally, angering the king — and he went through with it anyway. The source records that he foresaw beforehand that Jin Bi might not obey and would then have to be killed; as for the other costs, such as stealing the tally and angering the king, the source does not say whether he weighed them beforehand.

paras.zh: 第三处是事后的账。门客那句「於趙則有功矣，於魏則未為忠臣也」把两边算清：功劳是赵国的，亏欠是魏国的。原文记他受劝后立即自责，又在赵王面前侧行辞让，自言负魏、无功于赵，赵王因此终未献五城。至于留赵，原文把它紧接在魏王之怒与「公子亦自知也」之后；后文又记他「留趙十年不歸」，魏王派使者来请时，他「恐其怒之」，告诫门下敢替魏王使者通报者死；直到毛公、薛公往见，责他魏急而不恤，他才「立變色，告車趣駕歸救魏」，魏王见到他，两人相对而泣，魏王授他上将军印。事情并没有停在这里：秦王行金万斤于魏，求晋鄙的门客在魏王面前毁谤公子；魏王日闻其毁，不能不信，后来果然使人代公子将；公子自知再以毁废，谢病不朝，与宾客长夜饮，日夜为乐饮者四岁，「竟病酒而卒」。作者的一种解释是，秦国专找「晉鄙客」来毁谤，矫杀晋鄙这笔账最终也落回到他自己身上；原文并未明说两者之间的关联。至于留赵，一种解释是，他以留在赵国、不回魏国的方式认下了这笔债；但照原文，留赵也可能出于躲避魏王之怒，这一解读只能存疑。作者认为，他真正把这笔债说出口，是辞让五城时自言负魏的那一刻。
paras.en: The third is the accounting afterward. The retainer's words — in translation, a service to Zhao but not the act of a loyal minister to Wei — keep both columns straight: the credit belongs to Zhao, the debt to Wei. The source records that he blamed himself at once when rebuked, and that before the king of Zhao he stepped aside and declined, saying he had wronged Wei and had no merit in Zhao, so that the king never offered the five cities. As for staying in Zhao, the source places it directly after the king of Wei's anger and the note that the prince knew of it; later it records that he stayed in Zhao for ten years without returning, and that when the king of Wei sent envoys to ask for him, he feared the king's anger and warned his household that anyone who passed on a message from the king's envoys would die. Only when Mao Gong and Xue Gong went to see him and rebuked him for ignoring Wei in its peril did he, in translation, change countenance at once and order his carriage readied to go home and save Wei; on seeing him, the king of Wei wept with him and gave him the seal of supreme general. The story does not end there: the king of Qin spent ten thousand jin of gold in Wei, seeking out Jin Bi's former retainers to slander the prince to the king of Wei; hearing the slander daily, the king could not help believing it, and in the end had someone else replace the prince in command; knowing he had been cast aside by slander a second time, the prince pleaded illness and stayed away from court, drinking through the nights with his guests, carousing day and night for four years, until, in translation, he finally died of drink. One reading the author offers is that by Qin's seeking out Jin Bi's own retainers to do the slandering, the account of killing Jin Bi on a forged order came back to rest on the prince himself; the source does not state any such connection. As for staying in Zhao, one reading is that he acknowledged the debt by staying there rather than returning to Wei; but on the source's own account, staying in Zhao may equally have been a way of avoiding the king's anger, so that reading must remain tentative. In the author's view, the moment he actually spoke the debt aloud was when he declined the five cities and admitted he had wronged Wei.

paras.zh: 今天最常见的版本是：团队看到明显风险，决策层迟迟不动。假设你已经在正常渠道反复争取过，仍然没有结果；你手里有一线证据，也有一个能干的人。先别急着感动自己——照侯生的话问一句，我这个动作是解决问题，还是拿肉投餒虎？如果只是冲出去把话说完、把人得罪完，而风险一点没减，那叫白送。
paras.en: The commonest modern version: a team sees a clear risk, while the people with authority will not move. Suppose you have already pushed through the proper channels again and again, with no result; you hold a piece of hard evidence and you know a capable person. Before you start admiring your own nerve, put Hou Ying's question to your plan: is this move solving the problem, or throwing meat to a starving tiger? If all it does is get you out there to say your piece and offend everyone while the risk sits exactly where it was, that is a free throwaway.

paras.zh: 若决定动手，就把“对方不配合”写进计划：谁在什么情况下顶上，最坏的结果谁兜，留下什么记录。事情成了、庆功的时候，别急着站到中间：被绕过的流程、替你签字的人、被架空的上级，都是一笔账。把“于某处有功、于某处未为忠”先自己说出口，比等别人替你说体面得多。
paras.en: If you decide to act, write "the other side may not cooperate" into the plan: who steps in under which circumstances, who covers the worst outcome, what record stays behind. And when it works and the celebration starts, do not rush to stand in the middle. The process you bypassed, the person who signed for you, the superior you left out of the loop — all of that is an account. Saying it yourself first — a service here, a disloyalty there — is far more dignified than waiting for someone else to say it for you.

heading.en: Where Not to Take It at Face Value

paras.zh: 先说史源。本文只依据并核对了《史记·魏公子列传》一篇，未与其他记载对照。文中的对话与献计，如侯嬴献窃符之计、朱亥答话，是史家的记述，未必逐字。公子的「心不快」「意驕矜」「立自責」都是叙述用语，不是实录的心理。纪年照原文写魏安釐王二十年，不换算公元。
paras.en: Start with the sources. This piece relies on, and was checked against, one chapter only — the Biography of the Wei Prince in the Records of the Grand Historian — without comparison to other accounts. The dialogue and the proposed scheme — Hou Ying's plan to steal the tally, Zhu Hai's reply — are the historian's rendering and need not be verbatim. The prince's displeasure, self-congratulation and self-blame, as the narrative describes them, are narrative labels, not recorded psychology. The year is given as the twentieth of King Anxi of Wei, as the source has it, with no conversion to the common era.

paras.zh: 细节上更该存疑的是：「得選兵八萬人」在本篇只出现一次，本文未与其他记载对照；侯生自刭，原文记他此前说过「老臣不能從」，又自言「北鄉自剄，以送公子」，除此之外的动机，本文不作推测。
paras.en: The detail most worth doubting: the figure of eighty thousand picked men appears only once in this chapter, and this piece has not compared it with other accounts; as for Hou Ying cutting his throat, the source records that he had earlier said this old servant could not follow, and that he himself said he would face north and cut his throat to see the prince off; beyond that, this piece does not speculate about his motives.

scenario.zh: 小区电梯多次故障，你拿到一份检测报告，写明主板隐患明显；物业经理因怕得罪开发商不肯停用报修，只答应“再观察”。邻居里有一位相熟的电梯维修工愿意帮忙，但走正常报批要等一个月。
scenario.en: The elevator in your building has broken down several times. You have an inspection report stating plainly that the main control board is dangerously defective. The property manager, afraid of offending the developer, refuses to take the elevator out of service for repairs and will only agree to "keep watching it." Among the residents is an elevator technician you know who is willing to help — but going through the proper approval route would take a month.

question.zh: 在“上面不动、下面要出事”的局面里，你会不会绕过物业直接动手？动手之前，你会先备好什么，来对付“对方不配合”这一步？事成之后，你打算怎么向物业和被绕过的规则交代这笔账？
question.en: In a situation where those above will not move and those below are heading for an accident, would you bypass the property manager and act directly? Before acting, what would you prepare in advance to handle the step where "the other side does not cooperate"? And once it is done, how do you account to the property manager and to the rules you bypassed?

assumptions.zh:
隐患是真的，且有书面检测报告可留证
维修工愿意帮忙，但无授权，动手即属违规
物业不会主动认错，也不会替你担责
assumptions.en:
The defect is real, and the written inspection report can be kept as evidence
The technician is willing to help, but has no authorization; acting without it is a violation
The property manager will not admit fault, and will not take responsibility for you

steps.zh:
先判性质：直接停用或硬闯，是不是侯生说的“以肉投餒虎”——无人配合、报告不被承认，风险一点没减
为坏情况备预案：维修工到场而物业阻拦时，谁签字、谁见证、保留什么记录
把代价列清：可能被追责的人名单，以及最坏结果由谁兜
事成后不居功，主动承认绕过流程这笔亏欠，把整改记录和检测报告一并交给物业归档
steps.en:
Judge the nature of the act first: shutting it down by force, or barging in — is that Hou Ying's "meat thrown to a starving tiger"? If nobody cooperates and the report is not accepted, the risk has not shrunk at all
Prepare for the bad case: if the technician arrives and the property manager blocks the work, who signs, who witnesses, what records are preserved
Lay out the costs clearly: the list of people who might be held responsible, and who covers the worst outcome
Afterwards, do not claim credit; volunteer the admission that you bypassed procedure, and hand the repair records and the inspection report to the property manager for filing

alternative.zh: 作者提出的替代选择：先把报告公开给全体业主，把风险转成集体决定，用共同压力替个人冒险。代价是慢，可能来不及；好处是不必由一个人背“矫令杀将”的账。
alternative.en: The author's proposed alternative: publish the report to all the owners first, turning the risk into a collective decision and using shared pressure instead of personal daring. The cost is slowness — it may come too late; the benefit is that no single person has to carry the account of "forging the order and killing the general."

uncertainty_note.zh: 本篇只依据并核对了《史记·魏公子列传》一篇，未与他书对照；对话与献计是史家记述，未必逐字；「心不快」「意驕矜」「立自責」是叙述用语而非实录心理；不换算公元年份；「得選兵八萬人」在本篇只出现一次。
uncertainty_note.en: This piece relies on, and was checked against, one chapter only (the Biography of the Wei Prince in the Records of the Grand Historian), without comparison to other works. The dialogue and the proposed scheme are the historian's rendering and need not be verbatim; the prince's displeasure, self-congratulation and self-blame are narrative labels rather than recorded psychology; years are not converted to the common era; the figure of eighty thousand picked men appears only once in this chapter.

preheader.zh: 偷符之前，他先折回去问了看门的老头一句
preheader.en: Before stealing the tally, he turned back and asked the old gatekeeper one question
